headline: skills.sh ranking is install-ordered (2.2-2.8% rank/install inversion), so H107's token-naming premise is falsified; lane choice should be by install gate (13 / 24 / 1180 installs for top-10), not by token vacancy.
claim: Rank is a near-deterministic function of install count, not path-token similarity: the sole token-literal row in 'research report workflow' has 1 install and ranks 50, and 'competitive analysis report' has 0/177 token-literal rows yet a full token-untouched top-10. Reachable top-10 therefore depends on the lane's install gate - 13 installs in the 27-row 'market research playbook' lane, ~24 in 'research report workflow', ~1,180 in 'competitive analysis report'.
method: skills.sh search API (limit 200) probed 14:38-14:39Z for three deliverable-named queries; all aggregation (inversion%, install-sorted rank, token coverage, install histograms, install gates at ranks 1/5/10/20/50/100/150, top-10 owner mix) computed inside scripts on parsed JSON only - no raw bodies returned to context; our repo footprint via repo search endpoint.
implications: H107's token-naming lever is falsified; the install gate is the only ranking lever, and it differs by 90x across the three lanes (13 / 24 / 1180).
Lane selection is the strategic decision: play the 27-row playbook lane first, hold the 1,180-install competitive lane.
Any publish must ship with a distribution motion; a bare literal slug with 1-2 installs stays bottom-decile in large lanes.
KPI should be installs per listing per week; rank is a derived readout, not a target.
operational_actions: Push install distribution into the 13-install-gate lane (market research playbook), then the 24-install lane (research report workflow); hold competitive analysis report.
If publishing, publish themed slug + install motion together, never slug alone.
Instrument per-listing install counts weekly; compare against the lane gate table.
Mirror the competitor cluster pattern: multiple themed slugs from one publisher inside one lane.

falsifiers.F-a: listing with >=13 installs in the 27-row playbook lane still ranks >10 -> install ordering incomplete, relevance term exists
falsifiers.F-b: fresh literal slug with 0-2 installs reaches rank <=10 -> naming gate real, H107 reinstated
falsifiers.F-c: competitor with 0-2 installs holds a top-10 slot in a large lane -> authority/token factors dominate installs
falsifiers.F-d: our install counts stay pinned at 1 across two index refreshes -> constraint is reach/distribution, pivot to install mechanics

risks: Listing churn 29%/25h (cycle 107) still applies to listings we push installs into.
Prior-cycle premise correction: token-naming hypothesis (H107) is retired, not replaced by another naming variant.
Gate thresholds are snapshots at 14:39Z and drift with churn; re-measure gates, not ranks.
